speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry will start monitoring the number of employers who have adopted measures in the Tripartite Advisory for Managing Workplace Harassment, with such monitoring to include whether the employer has a policy explicitly defining harassment, including sexual harassment, whether the policy details how harassment will be dealt with, and whether training is provided to employees on how to prevent and respond to harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If the facts suggest that an offence under the Penal Code or the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) is committed, TAFEP will refer them to the Police or the Courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In 2015, the tripartite partners also agreed on a Tripartite Advisory on Managing Workplace Harassment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The tripartite partners affirm that all employers are expected to provide a safe and healthy working environment for their employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They are also in agreement that for cases that do not constitute a criminal offence, the proper way to deal with it is through effective grievance handling procedures within the companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To help employers put in place processes to prevent and manage workplace harassment complaints, TAFEP provides online resources, such as a sample workplace harassment prevention policy and a list of training providers, to train the supervisors in dealing with workplace harassment and complaints.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If the employer failed to address a workplace harassment case fairly, TAFEP would advise the employer to review the case again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: TAFEP would also engage the employer to put in place the proper measures as outlined in the Tripartite Advisory to ensure better prevention and also management of workplace harassment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I understand the Ministry is taking this issue very seriously.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The main concern here is that if we are not putting in some effort to try to track, for example, the number of employers who are adhering to these guidelines, we would find it difficult to say anything credibly about how well we are addressing these concerns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If there were, for example, an incident of severe workplace harassment, let us say, not taken care of properly in the workplace, as what happened to students at the National University of Singapore, then it would be difficult for the Government to say what is the actual state of affairs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Assoc Prof Walter Theseira for the supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Maybe allow me to explain what the difference is between a tripartite advisory and a tripartite standard.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But before that, allow me to again recap that two months ago, MOM announced that TAFEP will be made a resource centre of workplace harassment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One of the objectives is, like what Assoc Prof Walter Theseira has mentioned, to educate and also equip not just employers, but also employees, with the necessary information and resources when it comes to this topic of workplace harassment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the Tripartite Advisory, we have provided very clear, very comprehensive and a free sample copy of the Workplace Harassment Prevention Policy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Very detailed information, which will cover guiding principles, definition of workplace harassment and also how to take pre-emptive steps and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: TAFEP has also, within the last two months, produced a video, so that we can share with, not just employers but also employees, what constitutes workplace harassment, the definition I talked about; and the video outlines what the employers' fundamental responsibilities and policies should be.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that TAFEP is certainly stepping up efforts to extend the outreach to more employers and employees and also to advise more employers to implement the measures that are outlined in the tripartite advisory.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other than the education efforts, we are working with partners like the Labour Movement.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are also working with the Singapore National Employers' Federation to organise workshops because we realised it is not just the boss in the company, we need to work with the supervisors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And the workshops are also targeted at the supervisors to help them understand how to smoothen the employer and employee relationship.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The objective of the advisory is to outline the comprehensive information and also a sample copy of the Workplace Harassment Prevention Policy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is also a way for us to develop the pipeline for companies that will come on board the Tripartite Standards.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: TAFEP has carried ads about the Tripartite Standard on grievance handling so as to encourage employers to adopt proper and specific practices in these areas, which also include workplace harassment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As at end January this year, more than 960 employers – which collectively employ more than 498,000 people – have signed on to the standard.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Just a point and a suggestion for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Patrick Tay for the suggestion and I also want to take the opportunity to thank him and the Labour Members in the National Trades Union Congress Labour Movement for their efforts since the introduction of POHA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They have been doing very regular legal primers on this topic of workplace harassment in partnership with the Law Society of Singapore; they have done this since POHA was passed as law.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I know that they have done this to better educate the employees, in particular, the union members and the non-union members as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To answer the Member's question, this is a copy of the tripartite advisory.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOM and TAFEP will continue to work with our tripartite partners to keep this document current and relevant.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I must also say that the current focus is to go all out, to expand our outreach to cover even more employers and employees.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We remain committed to keep this current and relevant, so that we can advise and bring on board more employers to keep our workplaces harassment-free.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary earlier mentioned that a centre will be set up for employees to report cases of sexual harassment at the workplace.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: That is not coming yet, that is actually in the pipeline.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share more of that and what is the process for employees to come forward if they want to report cases at the centre?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to share the functions of the Resource Centre.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For affected employees who need counselling services, TAFEP will also help advise them on where to obtain such support services and put them in touch with the relevant agencies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we also provide them the necessary support.
